A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AnySat and contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices A–D. Corresponding material can be matched reliably despite rewriting, additions, and table relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification, segmentation, deforestation detection, linear-probing, and ablation results in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds evaluations on So2Sat and HLS Burn Scar.

M1.justification: Section 3.3 adds adaptation to unseen sensors by randomly initializing and training a new projector, used for HLS. The reported missing-channel padding changes from a value shared across sensors to a sensor-specific scalar. The core JEPA architecture, losses, and modality fusion remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 retains the five GeoPlex datasets and four original external datasets, adding So2Sat urban local-climate-zone classification and HLS Burn Scar segmentation. These extend evaluation to a new application domain, previously untrained HLS inputs, and substantially larger individual tiles.

E2.justification: Prithvi-EO-2.0, labelled Prithvi2, is added as a comparator on Sen1Floods11 and HLS Burn Scar in v2 Table B. The existing GeoPlex comparator sets and earlier external comparator families are retained.

E3.justification: v2 adds full-fine-tuning comparisons on Sen1Floods11, including CROMA with 350M and Prithvi with 130M trainable parameters. New evaluations include So2Sat linear probing with 29K parameters and HLS fine-tuning plus a configuration labelled linear probing with 3M parameters. Existing split and optimization descriptions remain; these additions do not establish reruns of retained experiments.

E4.justification: The HLS experiment adds a targeted cross-sensor transfer test using imagery absent from GeoPlex and a newly trained projector. The original random-dropping, contrastive-loss, subpatch-feature, and modality/temporal-masking ablations remain unchanged, as do the qualitative example cases.

E5.justification: Neither version supplies repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Both report point estimates and retain the same qualitative attribution of FLAIR variation to stochastic noise.

E6.justification: v2 Table B adds HLS results of 90.6 mIoU after fine-tuning and 87.7 for the 3M-parameter probing configuration, and So2Sat accuracy of 59.1 versus DOFA's 59.3. It also adds Sen1Floods11 comparison entries and revises Prithvi-UperNet from 90.4 to 88.3, reporting 90.4 separately for full fine-tuning. These are additions and reporting revisions; retained AnySat benchmark and ablation scores are unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(5) and Appendix equation (A) retain the same mathematics. Figure 2 introduces equivalent notation, Delta_m = P/R_m. No theoretical results, proofs, or formal guarantees are added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract replaces 'better or near state-of-the-art' after fine-tuning with an unqualified state-of-the-art claim after fine-tuning or probing, extending external coverage from four datasets to six. The introduction explicitly claims generalization to unseen sensor configurations. The principal AnySat, JEPA, and GeoPlex contributions remain.

C2.justification: v2 interprets HLS performance as evidence of transfer beyond the pretraining sensors despite Prithvi's much larger HLS pretraining corpus. Section 3.3 adds an applicability boundary: sufficiently different sensors require projector training and cannot simply be probed. Earlier interpretations of masking and the benefits of pretraining are retained.

D1.justification: Table C and Appendix D add sample counts, resolutions, channels, and patch sizes for the new datasets; FLAIR's reported pixel count changes from 24 to 20 GPix. Conversely, v2 removes baseline fusion, temporal-input selection, and backbone-selection details, along with the PANGAEA result-source disclosure. Core hardware, optimizer, and code/model availability information remains.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for So2Sat, HLS Burn Scar, and Prithvi-EO-2.0, while removing FlexiViT, Perceiver, PANGAEA, and the UPerNet reference. The related-work discussion remains largely unchanged. Section 4.2 drops v1's claim to be the first EO model effectively linearly probed for semantic segmentation.

P1.justification: Substantial portions of Sections 3.1–3.3 are rewritten and condensed, including patch encoding, the student–teacher description, and downstream prediction. The evaluation narrative is reorganized, with separate probing and new-sensor discussions. The title is also revised. This constitutes extensive editorial restructuring despite stable core mathematics.

P2.justification: Figures 4, 5, and A gain dataset markers, panels, or spokes; Figure 2's notation and caption change. Figure B retains its images but swaps the prediction and ground-truth labels. v1 Table 1 moves to the appendix as expanded Table B, while the dataset table becomes Table C. The overall visual format is retained.

improvement.justification: The new HLS experiment tests a previously unevaluated sensor-transfer capability, and So2Sat broadens application evidence. However, v2 removes baseline protocol and provenance details and strengthens superiority claims despite Table B reporting So2Sat accuracy below DOFA, 59.1 versus 59.3. These substantive gains and reporting regressions prevent a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
